items.title: The Conway polynomial

references.title: Introduction to Vassiliev Knot Invariants, §2.3
Polyak–Viro Formulas for Coefficients of the Conway Polynomial, §§3.4–4.2
Elementary proof of existence of the Alexander-Conway polynomial, §§1–4, PDF pp. 1–9

items.statement:
For an oriented link type $L$ in $S^3$, the Conway polynomial is the polynomial $
abla_L(z)\in\mathbb Z[z]$ characterized by the normalization $
abla_U(z)=1$ for the unknot $U$ and the skein relation
$$
abla_{L_+}(z)-
abla_{L_-}(z)=z\,
abla_{L_0}(z).$$
Here $L_+$ and $L_-$ are identical oriented links outside a ball and have respectively a positive and negative crossing inside it, while $L_0$ is obtained in that ball by the orientation-preserving smoothing. For each integer $k\ge0$, the $k$th Conway coefficient is $c_k(L):=[z^k]
abla_L(z)$. This carrier records the conventional skein interface; existence and uniqueness of the invariant are a separate well-definedness obligation. The skein characterization is on nonempty oriented links. If the link domain also includes the empty link, extend the invariant by the separate conventional value $
abla_{\varnothing}(z)=0$; this empty-link value is not determined by the nonempty skein axioms.

items.title: The Kontsevich integral on parenthesized braids

references.title: Introduction to Vassiliev Knot Invariants, §§8.2, 8.5–8.8, and 10.1
The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants, §§2.3–2.5
The Universal Vassiliev–Kontsevich Invariant for Framed Oriented Links

items.statement:
Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For a parenthesized braid path $\gamma$ in the configuration space of $q$ distinct complex points, define its Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) series by the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy of
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j).$$
Explicitly, if $\gamma:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ is an ordinary path with noncolliding endpoints, its holonomy is
$$1+\sum_{m\ge1}\int_{0<t_m<\cdots<t_1<1}\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_1)\cdots\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_m).$$
A tangential endpoint is a limiting collision configuration together with a specified nonzero first-order direction of approach for each colliding cluster. When endpoints have such clusters prescribed by the parenthesizations, the holonomy is the constant term after removing the local logarithmic factors $\exp(t_{ij}\log\varepsilon/(2\pi i))$ at each tangential endpoint. A change between the two parenthesizations of three consecutive strands is encoded by the regularized transport $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

For parenthesized braids the KZ holonomy takes values in the framed strand algebra, where only tangled 4T is imposed; passing from a closed framed strand diagram to an unframed knot applies the quotient by isolated-chord 1T. Fix a standard hump $H$ by starting with the two-critical-point unknot and inserting one local birth of a maximum-minimum pair; thus $H$ has two local maxima. The normalized unframed Kontsevich series of $K$ is
$$
I(K):=Z(K)\,Z(H)^{-r(K)}\in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C},
$$
The normalization uses one copy of $Z(H)$ for each local maximum; its degree-zero term is $1$, so its inverse is interpreted in the product completion. This definition makes no assertion that the unnormalized KZ coefficients are rational or that equal Kontsevich series separate knot types.

The following figure illustrates the positive Artin generator $\sigma_1$ and parenthesization conventions. Height increases upward, the right-bottom strand is the overstrand under the determinant crossing convention, and the labels at the ends record the ordered parenthesizations; no proof below relies on the drawing.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.82,thick]
  \draw (2,0) -- (2,3);
  \draw[very thick] (1,0) -- (0.5,1.5) -- (0,3);
```

items.statement:
For every integer $q\ge2$, let $\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ be the space of ordered $q$-tuples of pairwise distinct complex points, and let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ and $t_{ij}$ be as defined for parenthesized braids. Write $\sigma_i$ for the positive geometric half twist interchanging adjacent strands $i$ and $i+1$ in a disk containing no other strand. The Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov form
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j)$$
satisfies $d\Omega_q=0$ and $\Omega_q\wedge\Omega_q=0$. Consequently the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy depends only on the homotopy class of a path with fixed endpoints. On geometric braids this holonomy respects the distant commutation relations $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i$ for $|i-j|\ge2$ and the adjacent braid relations $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$.

items.statement:
Let $T_1\subset\mathbb C\times[a,c]$ and $T_2\subset\mathbb C\times[c,b]$ be compact strict Morse tangles whose boundary points and orientations match at the regular level $c$, with the joined tangle $T=T_2\circ T_1$ smooth and embedded. Their unframed configuration integrals converge absolutely degreewise and satisfy
$$
Z(T_2\circ T_1)=Z(T_2)\,Z(T_1),
$$
where multiplication stacks tangle diagrams with $T_2$ above $T_1$. The equality holds in the completed unframed tangle diagram space and uses only the finite-degree integrals defined on the matched pieces.

items.title: Tangential KZ regularization and the hump normalization

references.title: Introduction to Vassiliev Knot Invariants, §§8.4, 8.6–8.7, and 10.1.5–10.1.7
The Universal Vassiliev–Kontsevich Invariant for Framed Oriented Links, §4

items.statement:
For each finite degree cutoff $N$, every parenthesized endpoint cluster of the KZ connection has a unique coefficientwise tangentially regularized transport, obtained by removing its local residue factor. For three strands, fix the normalized positions $(0,z,1)$ and put $a=t_{12}/(2\pi i)$ and $b=t_{23}/(2\pi i)$. The equation $G'(z)=\left(\frac{a}{z}+\frac{b}{z-1}\right)G(z)$ has unique solutions $G_0,G_1$ with $G_0(z)=f(z)z^a$, $G_1(z)=g(1-z)(1-z)^b$, where $f$ and $g$ are analytic near $0$ and $f(0)=g(0)=1$. Their ratio $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}:=G_1(z)^{-1}G_0(z)$ is independent of $z$ and equals the regularized limit $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\varepsilon^{-b}G_\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\varepsilon^a,\qquad G_\varepsilon(\varepsilon)=1$.
If $K^+$ is obtained from a strict Morse knot presentation $K$ by inserting one copy of the fixed standard hump $H$, model the local birth by cutting the knot to a one-in one-out tangle $T_K$, composing with the standard one-in one-out hump tangle whose closure is $H$, and closing the composite. Then $Z(K^+)=Z(H)Z(K)$, $r(K^+)=r(K)+1$, and hence $I(K^+)=I(K)$. The inverse in $I(K)$ exists degreewise because the degree-zero coefficient of $Z(H)$ is $1$. The associator identities and independence under arbitrary changes of parenthesization are separate claims.

items.statement: Assume countable choice, and let $I_m(K)$ be the degree-$m$ homogeneous coefficient of the normalized unframed Kontsevich series $I(K)$ of a smooth oriented knot type $K$. For $n\ge0$, put $I_{\le n}(K)=\sum_{m=0}^{n}I_m(K)$. A function on knot types is of type at most $n$ when its alternating resolution sum on every $(n+1)$-singular knot is zero. Then $I_{\le n}$ is a type-at-most-$n$ invariant with values in the sum of the unframed degree-$m$ chord-diagram modules for $0\le m\le n$. For every $n$-singular knot with chord diagram $D$, its $n$-fold finite difference satisfies $D_n I_{\le n}(K)=D$. In particular, the degree-$n$ symbol is the identity on rational chord diagrams after extending scalars to $\mathbb C$; no rational-coefficient claim is made about $I_m(K)$.

items.title: Universality of the Kontsevich integral

references.title: Introduction to Vassiliev Knot Invariants, §8.8.1
The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants, §§1.1 and 2.6

items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}$ be the $\mathbb C$-vector space of ambient-isotopy invariants of oriented knots with values in $\mathbb C$ and type at most $n$, where type at most $n$ means that the alternating resolution sum on every $(n+1)$-singular knot is zero; set $\mathcal V_{-1}^{\mathbb C}=0$. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be the rational vector space on degree-$n$ circle chord diagrams modulo 4T and 1T; a weight system is a $\mathbb Q$-linear functional on this space. For an $n$-singular knot with chord diagram $D$, define $\sigma_n([V])(D)$ to be the $n$-fold alternating resolution sum of $V$ on that knot. Let $I_{\le n}(K)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}I_j(K)$ be the degree-$n$ truncation of the normalized unframed Kontsevich series. The degree-$n$ symbol map
$$
\sigma_n:\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}/\mathcal V_{n-1}^{\mathbb C}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}},\mathbb C)
$$
is surjective. In particular, every rational weight system has a complex-valued finite-type lift; no rationality claim is made about that lift or about the coefficients of $I(K)$. Moreover, for every $n$ and every $V\in\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}$ there is a complex-linear functional $\Lambda_V$ on $\bigoplus_{j=0}^{n}(\mathcal A_j^{\mathrm{un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$ whose degree-$n$ restriction is the degree-$n$ symbol of $V$ and such that
$$
V(K)=\Lambda_V(I_{\le n}(K))
$$
for every oriented knot type $K$. This recovery statement does not imply that distinct knot types have distinct Kontsevich series.
